close_reason: Added bool_arg / take_bool_arg to jmap-server::helpers and re-exported from the crate root. Adopted in canonical mail-server (~21 sites: email.rs, mailbox.rs, submission.rs, sieve.rs) and calendars-server (~7 sites: calendar.rs, event.rs, principal.rs). Excluded ~5 Value-shaped inner-JSON reads in mail-server (bv_entry isEncodingProblem/isTruncated, sort comparator isAscending, build_mailbox_from_props isSubscribed, MDN keyword check) by design — different helper signature needed. cargo test passes across mail (247), calendars (82), jmap-server (106) crates. description:
The chained pattern for parsing an optional boolean JMAP arg is repeated 7 times in this crate:
  - event.rs:78-80 (reduceParticipants)
  - event.rs:196-200 (sendSchedulingMessages)
  - event.rs:560-563 (onSuccessDestroyOriginal)
  - event.rs:796-799 (calculateTotal)
  - event.rs:840-843 (expandRecurrences)
  - principal.rs:61-64 (showDetails)
  - calendar.rs:73-76 (onDestroyRemoveEvents)

Each site is the same shape:
  let flag = args
      .get("someKey")
      .and_then(|v| v.as_bool())
      .unwrap_or(false);

Workspace-wide this pattern is in 30+ sites across jmap-mail-server (13 in email.rs, 7 in mailbox.rs, 2 in submission.rs, 1 each in mdn.rs, sieve.rs) and jmap-calendars-server.

Idiomatic Rust would consolidate this into a small helper, either:
  pub(crate) fn bool_arg(args: &Map<String, Value>, key: &str, default: bool) -> bool {
      args.get(key).and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(default)
  }
or an extension trait:
  trait ArgsExt { fn bool_arg(&self, key: &str, default: bool) -> bool; }

A 4-line, three-method chain repeated 30+ times is a textbook case for extracting a helper. The helper site also gives one place to document the JMAP convention of 'silently coerce non-bool/missing to default' if that ever needs to change (RFC 8620 §3.6.1 permissive parsing).

Per the workspace canonical-template rule: fix the canonical jmap-mail-server first, then propagate to all 7 extension-server siblings in the same pass.
